Use the graph and symbolic rule to test: Instantaneous rate is the derivative at that point.
Correct a common Instantaneous Rate of Change mistake.
example: For f(x)=x^2, what is f'(2)?
misconception: Using a wide interval for an instant rate.

title: Derivative from First Principles
objectives: Define Derivative from First Principles.
Use the graph and symbolic rule to test: Start from [f(x+h)-f(x)]/h and take h to 0.
Correct a common Derivative from First Principles mistake.
example: Why not set h=0 immediately?
misconception: Putting h=0 before simplifying.

title: Implicit Differentiation
objectives: Define Implicit Differentiation.
Use the graph and symbolic rule to test: Treat y as a function of x, so d(y)/dx is y'.
Correct a common Implicit Differentiation mistake.
example: Differentiate y^2 with respect to x.
misconception: Differentiating y as if it were a constant.

example: If dy/dt=6 and dx/dt=2, find dy/dx.
misconception: Using dy/dt as dy/dx.

misconception: Treating the zero vector as an eigenvector because A0=lambda0.

title: Correlation Coefficient
objectives: Define Correlation Coefficient accurately.
Make a scatter plot, check that a linear pattern is sensible, then read r between -1 and 1.
Avoid this common mistake: Thinking correlation proves one variable causes the other.
example: A fair die. P(score ≤ 5)?
misconception: Thinking correlation proves one variable causes the other.

title: Addition Rule
objectives: Define Addition Rule accurately.
Add P(A) and P(B), then subtract P(A and B) if the events overlap.
Avoid this mistake: Adding overlapping events without subtracting the overlap.
example: A fair die. P(score ≤ 2)?
misconception: Adding overlapping events without subtracting the overlap.

title: Multiplication Rule
objectives: Define Multiplication Rule accurately.
Multiply P(A) by P(B after A), or multiply separate probabilities when events are independent.
Avoid this mistake: Multiplying as if events are independent when they are not.
example: A fair die. P(score ≤ 3)?
misconception: Multiplying as if events are independent when they are not.

Avoid this mistake: Thinking independent means the events cannot happen together.
example: Does one fair coin toss affect the next toss?
misconception: Thinking independent means the events cannot happen together.

title: Cumulative Distribution
objectives: Define Cumulative Distribution accurately.

misconception: Confusing P(X = x) with P(X <= x).

example: If z=6 and the critical value is 3, is |z| past the cutoff?
misconception: Using p-hat instead of the null proportion in the test standard error.

misconception: Thinking vertices need a direct edge to be in the same component.

title: Simple Interest
objectives: Explain Simple interest is calculated only on the original principal, so equal time periods add equal interest amounts.
Convert the percentage rate to a decimal, match the rate period to the time unit, compute I=Prt, and add the principal to obtain A=P+I.
Correct the misconception: Using P(1+r)^t for a simple-interest question.
example: Simple interest on 1000 at 5% for 2 years?
misconception: Using P(1+r)^t for a simple-interest question.

title: Invertible Functions
objectives: Define Invertible Functions correctly.

Avoid this mistake: Trying to invert a many-one function.

misconception: Trying to invert a many-one function.

title: Angle Between Line and Plane

Identify points, direction vectors, or normal vectors, then substitute them into the matching 3D geometry formula.

example: Compute this Angle Between Line and Plane case with input 2: A right angle is what fraction of a 360° turn? Labelled result 2 → 90.
misconception: Using coordinates as direction data without subtracting or checking the vector meaning.
